paragraphMoves.title: Scene → pattern → idea
paragraphMoves.description: Let a concept become useful through an encounter.
paragraphMoves.caution: Do not mistake one example for a universal pattern.

steps.label: Scene
steps.instruction: Show one specific moment in the current hall.
steps.bridge: Which relation can we notice?

steps.label: Pattern
steps.instruction: Identify a recurrence or relation, stating its limits.
steps.bridge: What concept makes this relation precise?

steps.label: Idea
steps.instruction: Name the concept and reconnect it to the scene.
steps.bridge: What can the reader now notice or test?

paragraphMoves.title: Claim → evidence → interpretation
paragraphMoves.description: Make a claim answer to something the reader can inspect.
paragraphMoves.caution: Evidence must support the actual claim; interpretation is not another observation.

steps.label: Claim
steps.bridge: What supports it?

steps.label: Evidence
steps.instruction: Point to a source, observation or reproducible result.
steps.bridge: What does this establish, and what remains uncertain?

steps.label: Interpretation
steps.instruction: Explain what the evidence changes about the claim.
steps.bridge: Why does that matter to the next passage?

paragraphMoves.title: Question → attempt → revision
paragraphMoves.description: Let understanding change inside the passage.
paragraphMoves.caution: Do not invent a foolish first answer merely to defeat it.

steps.label: Question
steps.instruction: Ask a question whose answer matters here.
steps.bridge: What is a plausible first answer?

steps.label: Attempt
steps.instruction: Try that answer against a concrete case.
steps.bridge: Which detail does it miss?

steps.label: Revision
steps.instruction: Revise only what the evidence requires.
steps.bridge: What can we now investigate more precisely?

paragraphMoves.title: Observation → implication
paragraphMoves.description: Follow a small fact into its consequence.
paragraphMoves.caution: Mark interpretation and uncertainty; avoid generalising beyond the observation.

steps.label: Observation
steps.instruction: Describe what happened and under which conditions.
steps.bridge: What follows from that observation?

steps.label: Implication
steps.instruction: Explain one consequence, with its limits.
steps.bridge: What action or question follows?

paragraphMoves.title: Topic → specification → implication
paragraphMoves.description: Narrow a subject before saying what follows.
paragraphMoves.caution: A broad topic sentence is optional; avoid introductory padding.

steps.label: Topic
steps.instruction: Name the relation this paragraph will clarify.
steps.bridge: Which exact case matters?

steps.label: Specification
steps.instruction: Supply a precise case or condition.
steps.bridge: What changes because of this detail?

steps.label: Implication
steps.instruction: Draw a bounded consequence for the reader.
steps.bridge: Where does this lead in the text?

paragraphMoves.title: Assertion → qualification
paragraphMoves.description: Keep a useful claim while making its scope honest.
paragraphMoves.caution: Qualification should clarify conditions, not drain every sentence of commitment.

steps.label: Assertion
steps.bridge: Under which conditions does it hold?

steps.label: Qualification
steps.instruction: Name a material limit, exception or dependency.
steps.bridge: What can be done within that boundary?

studies.author: Donna Haraway
studies.title: Situated Knowledges
studies.locator: pp. 580–581: final paragraph before The Persistence of Vision and its first two paragraphs.
studies.note: Local paragraph reading; attitudes and divisions are our interpretation.
studies.takeaway: A metaphor changes when the old one cannot carry the problem.
studies.caution: Keep the political stakes specific. A change of metaphor is not evidence by itself.

steps.observation: Competing commitments become an awkward bodily image.
steps.bridge: What must change in the framing?

steps.observation: Vision is reclaimed through embodiment; situated knowledge is named.
steps.bridge: What makes this account necessary?

steps.observation: An accumulating catalogue of instruments intensifies the critique of unrestricted sight.
steps.bridge: Which specific viewpoint can we account for?

adaptation.title: Change the frame when it stops helping
adaptation.description: An Ada proposal for a passage whose familiar metaphor conceals a condition.
instructions: Name a genuine tension in the hall and show why the familiar description cannot resolve it.
Offer a more precise frame, define it, and identify what it makes visible.
Test that frame against concrete mechanisms and their stakes; end with an accountable viewpoint.

studies.author: Gilles Deleuze and Félix Guattari
studies.title: A Thousand Plateaus — Introduction: Rhizome
studies.edition: Brian Massumi translation, University of Minnesota Press, 1987.
studies.locator: Opening three prose paragraphs, printed pp. 3–5.
studies.note: Paragraphs span pages. This is a local argumentative route, not the structure of the entire book.
studies.takeaway: The opening performs a disturbance before turning it into a way of reading.
studies.caution: Do not treat connection alone as explanation or present their philosophy as OOO.

steps.observation: The two named writers present authorship as already multiple.
steps.bridge: What else seemed singular?

steps.observation: The book becomes an assemblage; questions turn toward its connections and effects.
steps.bridge: How can writing follow those relations?

steps.observation: A conceptual inventory leads into writing understood as mapping.
steps.bridge: What would this method attend to next?

adaptation.title: From one object to its relations
adaptation.description: An Ada proposal that shifts attention from a named object to what it does with others.
instructions: Begin with an actual object whose apparent unity is complicated by its operation.
Follow two consequential connections; explain each mechanism and what the connection changes.
Name the resulting method of inquiry and set a concrete next investigation.

studies.author: Sara Ahmed
studies.title: Queer Phenomenology — Introduction: Find Your Way
studies.locator: Printed pp. 3–4: orientation, the writing table, and bringing its support forward.
studies.note: Checked against the previously downloaded PDF. The public URL returned 403 during this pass.
studies.takeaway: A condition of thinking becomes the subject of thought.
studies.caution: Keep Ahmed's queer phenomenology distinct from OOO; examine whose orientation is being treated as ordinary.

steps.observation: Orientation leads to the table nearest the philosopher.
steps.bridge: Why is this object nearby?

steps.observation: Furniture supports the place and practice of philosophy.
steps.bridge: Why does support disappear from attention?

steps.observation: The background table is deliberately brought into the argument's foreground.
steps.bridge: What becomes visible from this changed angle?

adaptation.title: Bring the support into view
adaptation.description: An Ada proposal for examining what quietly makes an encounter possible.
instructions: Locate the reader and a nearby object; say what directs attention toward it.
Follow one actual supporting arrangement: surface, code, access or labour.
Bring that support into the foreground and show what changes in the original encounter.

studies.author: Friedrich Kittler
studies.title: Gramophone, Film, Typewriter — Introduction
studies.edition: Geoffrey Winthrop-Young and Michael Wutz translation; Stanford course transcription (header dated 1997).
studies.locator: First seven paragraphs, from optical-fibre networks to the return to still-distinct media.
studies.note: Some adjacent paragraphs are grouped into movements. Predictions belong to the source's historical moment.
studies.takeaway: A technical forecast opens into military infrastructure, everyday pleasure and a temporal correction.
studies.caution: Check present-day technical claims independently. Polemical scale can outrun the evidence.

steps.observation: A communications technology introduces a converging future.
steps.bridge: What condition underpins the promise?

steps.observation: Resistance to interference leads into military planning.
steps.bridge: Where does ordinary experience enter?

steps.observation: Domestic entertainment appears as a secondary benefit.
steps.bridge: What larger conclusion is being drawn?

steps.observation: A sweeping digital forecast is interrupted by existing media.
steps.bridge: What history explains the present arrangement?

adaptation.title: Follow an interface to its conditions
adaptation.description: An Ada proposal that traces a visible experience into technical and institutional conditions.
instructions: Start with one concrete operation the student encounters.
Trace a verified dependency behind it and identify a relevant historical condition.
Return to what that arrangement permits the player to experience.
Separate the observed present from a projected future; carry the distinction forward.

studies.author: Gaston Bachelard
studies.title: The Poetics of Space — The House
studies.edition: Maria Jolas translation; Beacon edition with 1994 foreword.
studies.locator: Chapter I, printed pp. 3–5, first six prose paragraphs after the epigraph.
studies.note: Adjacent paragraphs are grouped; the epigraph is a separate reading event.
studies.takeaway: A familiar place changes scale through an inquiry into inhabiting it.
studies.caution: Do not assume that home is safe or universal. Keep memory and imagination distinct from measured mechanism.

steps.observation: The house becomes a problem of intimacy and images.
steps.bridge: What would an adequate account require?

steps.observation: Description gives way to a question about inhabiting.
steps.bridge: How far can this small place extend?

steps.observation: The house becomes a first world against distant abstraction.
steps.bridge: What enters a new place with its inhabitant?

steps.observation: Shelter opens into remembered houses and imagination.
steps.bridge: How does the present place now feel different?

adaptation.title: An inhabited detail widens
adaptation.description: An Ada proposal for a spatial passage that opens into memory without losing its present setting.
instructions: Begin with a specific place and a question about how it is inhabited.
Move from visible description to a concrete bodily relation.
Change the scale of attention while naming the limits of the analogy.
Bring a sourced or clearly imagined memory into relation with the present room; allow different experiences.

studies.author: Lewis Carroll
studies.title: Through the Looking-Glass — The Garden of Live Flowers
studies.locator: Chapter II opening path episode, then the later approach to the Red Queen.
studies.note: Two selected episodes; the intervening flower conversation is omitted from this analysis, not claimed absent.
studies.takeaway: Repeated attempts prepare a reversal that becomes legible through action.
studies.caution: A fictional rule is not a physics explanation. An Ada version needs a consistent, inspectable mechanism.

steps.observation: An ordinary destination meets a path that returns Alice home.
steps.bridge: Will a more deliberate attempt succeed?

steps.observation: Determination produces another return and an accusation against the house.
steps.bridge: What alternative action could work?

steps.locator: Later: advice from the Rose and Alice's first attempt
steps.observation: Counterintuitive advice is dismissed; approaching the Queen fails.
steps.bridge: What happens if the advice is tried?

steps.observation: Walking away succeeds where approaching failed.
steps.bridge: What rule can now be investigated?

adaptation.title: A rule discovered through failed attempts
adaptation.description: An Ada proposal for a bounded puzzle whose operation is learned through consequences.
instructions: Give the student a simple goal and show one understandable failed attempt.
Repeat with one meaningful variation; keep the mechanism consistent.
Offer a counterintuitive possibility and test the ordinary expectation.
Try the alternative, then explain precisely why this artifact permits the result.
